etymologies.etymologyHTML: From alteration of dialectal simper, from Middle English simperen (“to simmer”), of possibly imitative origin. First attested in the intransitive sense. The noun is from the verb. First attested in the late 15 century.

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To cook or undergo heating slowly at or below the boiling point. [from mid 17th c.]

quote.citation: 1945 January and February, “Notes and News: American Locomotives in France”, in Railway Magazine, page 46:
quote.text: The locomotive was the now inevitable American 2-8-0, No. 2623. There she stood, effectively blocking the level crossing, simmering gently, massively inert. It was almost dark, and one's final sight was of her high, firelit cab, the enginemen nonchalantly leaning out, waiting for the right-away, while impatient road convoys piled up on both sides of the crossing.

quote.citation: 2004, Susan Westmoreland, The Good Housekeeping Cookbook, Hearst Books, →ISBN, page 89:
quote.text: That way, the heat can circulate under the meat and prevent it from simmering in its juices.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To cause to cook or to cause to undergo heating slowly at or below the boiling point.

quote.citation: 1981, Phyllis Hobson, Easy Game Cookery, Storey Publishing, →ISBN, page 2:
quote.text: There are other easy ways you can bake and simmer and sauté wild game  without qualifying as a gourmet cook.

definitions.definition: (intransitive, figurative) To be on the point of breaking out into anger; to be agitated. [from 1760s]

quote.citation: 2006, Earl Ganz, The Taos Truth Game, UNM Press, →ISBN:
quote.text: Maybe that really did happen, and Robin's anger at his wife had simmered for this long?

definitions.definition: (intransitive, figurative) To remain angry with someone or something past the point of exhaustion; to resign oneself to holding a grudge, especially after some failed attempts to resolve a situation.
(intransitive, figurative) To develop gradually, of an idea or plan.

quote.citation: 2003, Mark H. Walker, Games That Sell!, Wordware Publishing, Inc., →ISBN, page 162:
quote.text: The idea for The Sims was one that had  been simmering in Wright's mind for quite some time, and was initially conceived as an architecture simulation.

definitions.definition: The state or process of simmering. [from early 19th c.]

etymologies.etymologyHTML: From sim (“simulation”, noun) +‎ -er.

definitions.definition: (informal, video games) Someone who plays a sim (a simulation game), particularly The Sims.
